gnosh mcp add

  Add a server. A server gnosh starts is its command and arguments; one at a
  URL is -t http and the URL. Put -- before the command when it has flags of
  its own.

  Not built yet in this build of gnosh: typing it stops with a message that
  says so.

Usage
  gnosh mcp add [flags] <name> <command-or-url> [args...]

Flags
  -s, --scope <scope>
      Where the server is kept: local (this project, for you alone: the
      default for add), user (every project of yours) or project (the
      project's .mcp.json, which goes with it). (Not built yet.)
  -t, --transport <transport>
      How the server is reached: stdio (gnosh starts it: the default) or http
      (it is at a URL). (Not built yet.)
  -e, --env <KEY=value...>
      Set these variables for a server gnosh starts. (Not built yet.)
  -H, --header <header...>
      Send these headers ("Name: value") to a server at a URL. (Not built
      yet.)
  --cwd <dir>
      Work in this folder instead of the current one.
  -h, --help
      Show help: gnosh's, or after a command's name that command's.
